authors: Ziming An; Mehdi Dagdoug; David Haziza; Yves Tillé
title: Agnostic Model-Assisted Estimation with Machine Learning for Survey Data
what_it_holds: Design-based model-assisted estimation with any ML learner and cross-fitting, units are the sampling units (no cluster or two-stage designs). Design-agnostic cross-fitting randomly partitions the population into folds; Theorem 1 gives conditional independence across folds exactly when the design given sample size is exponential (SRSWOR, Bernoulli, Poisson, conditional Poisson). Variance estimator from cross-fitted residuals (Theorem 8; reduces to Opsomer-Miller 2005 under leave-one-out) with asymptotic normal intervals; Godambe-Joshi bound. No t reference or few-unit correction and no separate cross-fitting variance term that escapes the fpc seen. [Read abstract page and an HTML summary; theorems not read in full; PDF unreadable through the fetch tool.]

authors: Riaño (first name and co-authors not verified)
title: Model-assisted estimation with a training subsample: a two-phase sampling approach with design-based variance estimation
date: Sept 2026 per brief and ID (after 1 Sep 2026)
what_it_holds: Treats the subsample used to train the prediction model as a second phase of sampling, giving an exact two-term design-based variance decomposition for any algorithm (second-phase term from the training partition plus the usual term). Shows single-partition estimator relates to its Rao-Blackwellized average; closed form second-phase variance for tree predictors; proposes analytic and replication variance estimators and 'budgeting the second phase' to restore near-nominal coverage in simulations. Setting is a probability sample of units; clusters, few units and t intervals not mentioned. [From abstract only, read through an aggregator summary; author list not seen.]

title: Machine learning methods for finite population parameter estimation in survey sampling
date: 2026 (month not shown on page; ID implies April 2026)
what_it_holds: Pedagogical review. Cross-fitting builds predictions from data not used to evaluate them; under Poisson sampling folds are formed before sampling and design-unbiasedness is immediate, under other designs the cross-fitted estimator is slightly biased unless conditional inclusion probabilities are used. Cross-fitted residuals give consistent variance estimators (HT form, Section 3.3; pseudo-value form, Section 4.3). Cluster and two-stage sampling not covered; two-phase appears only for unit nonresponse. [Read from an HTML summary of sections 3-5, not the full text.]

authors: Mehdi Dagdoug; Camelia Goga; David Haziza
title: Model-assisted estimation through random forests in finite population sampling
venue_or_arxiv: Journal of the American Statistical Association 118(542):1234-1251; DOI 10.1080/01621459.2021.1987250; arXiv:2002.09736
what_it_holds: Random-forest model-assisted estimators of totals and means, design-based theory and variance estimators, plus model calibration for several survey variables; simulations on bias, efficiency and CI coverage; Médiamétrie radio audience application. Per the Bouhadra-Dagdoug paper they introduced a cross-validated variance estimator. Units are sampling units with unequal-probability designs; clusters and few-unit t intervals not mentioned in the abstract. [From abstract only; cross-validated variance estimator detail relies on a secondary mention.]

title: PPI is the Difference Estimator: Recognizing the Survey Sampling Roots of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Argues the PPI mean estimator is the 1970s difference estimator and PPI+ is GREG. Design-based discussion assumes SRSWOR: variance (1-n/N) S_e^2 / n with S_e^2 the finite-population variance of residuals, and the fpc named explicitly. Mentions Cross-PPI sample splitting as a correction; no cluster or multistage designs and no cross-fitting variance term analysis. [From HTML summary of the article body.]

title: Model-Assisted Survey Estimation with Modern Prediction Techniques

authors: Xin Lü (listed as Xin Lu in text); Lei Shi; Hanzhong Liu; Peng Ding
title: Conditional cross-fitting for unbiased machine-learning-assisted covariate adjustment in randomized experiments
what_it_holds: Design-based, finite-population: potential outcomes fixed, randomization the only randomness; ATE under Bernoulli, completely randomized and stratified or matched-pair designs. Standard iid cross-fitting fails, so they split conditionally so each half is a randomized experiment given the split, and build a cross-fitted variance estimator from design-specific conservative HT-type variance estimators. Note An et al. cite a 'design-aware (Lu et al., 2025)' scheme, probably this paper (not confirmed). Experiments not survey clusters; the full variance estimator and guarantees were cut off in what I read. [Partial text.]

title: Cluster-Robust Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Cluster-robust PPI++ with closed-form SEs and asymptotic CIs under arbitrary within-cluster dependence, handling partially labelled clusters (some units labelled in each cluster), analysis of labelling design effect on precision, and a cluster-aware power-tuning rule; TV news application where plain PPI++ covered below 60%. Asymptotic; no small-cluster-count t correction, and superpopulation versus design-based framing and number of clusters studied not stated in what I saw. Bears on C3 (partial labelling inside clusters) but a level term or cluster intercept was not seen. [From abstract only.]

authors: Pranav Mani; Peng Xu; Zachary C. Lipton; Michael Oberst
title: No Free Lunch: Non-Asymptotic Analysis of Prediction-Powered Inference
what_it_holds: Exact finite-sample analysis for PPI++ mean estimation: PPI++ can be worse than classical inference when pseudo-label correlation is below about 1/sqrt(n-2) (Gaussian case); experiments with n below 50 compare single-sample and sample-splitting variants. Supports the concern about estimated coefficients at small n; iid labels, no clusters. [From abstract only.]

title: Regression for the Mean: Auto-Evaluation and Inference with Few Labels through Post-hoc Regression
what_it_holds: Argues PPI++ can underperform classical inference with few labels because the fitted coefficient has high variance (OLS analogy); proposes ridge and robust-regression coefficient estimation. Footnote notes fitting lambda on the labelled data can bias PPI at small n. iid, no clusters, no cross-fitting analysis. [From abstract and partial text.]

Empirical study (Mosaiks housing prices) shows double-dipping gives anti-conservative intervals. No clusters seen. [From abstract and partial text.]

what_it_holds: Replaces PPI's unweighted bias-correction term by an HT or Hájek weighted version so inference is valid under unequal labelling probabilities; propensities estimated from a model; simulations keep nominal coverage. Survey-sampling connection but units labelled independently, no clusters or cross-fitting variance. [From abstract only.]

title: Cross-Fitted Survey-Weighted TMLE with Design-Based Variance for Causal Machine Learning
what_it_holds: Stratified multistage survey design; cross-fits at the PSU level (whole PSUs assigned to folds, balanced within strata). Variance is the ultimate-cluster linearization estimator with an m_h/(m_h-1) adjustment, shown consistent. Simulation coverage about 0.93-0.95 cross-fitted versus 0.89-0.91 single-fit. TMLE for ATE, not PPI; asymptotic, no t reference and no analysis of a cross-fitting variance term outside the fpc. [From abstract and summary.]

authors: Salvador V. Balkus; Nima S. Hejazi; Hasan Laith
title: On the use of cross-fitting in causal machine learning with correlated units
what_it_holds: Shows that splitting as if units were independent still removes the key bias terms for clustered, spatial and time-series data, with simulations. Model-based (unrestricted statistical model) rather than finite-population; variance of cross-fitting and fpc not covered; number of clusters unspecified. [Partial text.]

title: On the two-phase framework for joint model and design-based inference
what_it_holds: Product probability space combining design and model randomness; asymptotic independence and joint convergence. Classical two-phase view of design plus model, no cross-fitting or cluster few-unit analysis. [From abstract summary.]

title: High-Dimensional Variance Estimation for the Generalized Regression Estimator
what_it_holds: GREG variance when p/n is not negligible: Taylor estimators under-estimate; a leave-one-out (cross-validated) variance estimator is asymptotically unbiased under Gaussian covariates and Bernoulli sampling (SRSWOR also simulated, N = 1000). Describes LOO as a special case of cross-validated variance in Dagdoug-Goga-Haziza 2023 and cross-fitted variance in An et al. Not cluster sampling. [From abstract and summary.]
